Arhinful 18 November 2026 5:26pm Former Finance Minister, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has challenged Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson to acknowledge what he describes as the failure of the government’s 24-hour economy initiative.
According to the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee, the government’s decision to move programmes previously associated with the 24-hour economy under its newly introduced New Economy policy raises questions about the continued relevance of the original initiative.
Speaking during the debate on the 2027 Budget in Parliament, Dr Amin Adam said he had expected the Finance Minister to admit that the 24-hour economy had not delivered on its promises.
“I was hoping that the Finance Minister would admit that the 24hr economy has failed after he moved all policies under the project to the new economy policy, he failed to do that,” he said.
He described the New Economy as a repackaging of programmes previously presented under the 24-hour economy, arguing that the restructuring had left the 24-hour economy secretariat with little justification for its continued existence.
He also questioned the allocation of GH¢165 million to the secretariat, saying the expenditure was an inappropriate use of public resources when the programmes it was expected to coordinate had been moved elsewhere.
“Taking all the programmes from the 24hr economy and putting them under the New Economy, the 24hr secretariat has nothing more to do. The Minister has allocated GH¢165m to the secretariat and I don’t think this is the way we should use our resources,” he added.
